object_context: Source-side determinant compactness/ground-state identification obstruction for the Riemann Hypothesis spectral lane. Starting from the Connes–Consani–Moscovici finite/restricted Weil-form construction, determine whether the actual lowest eigenfunction of QW_lambda (and its finite truncations) can be identified with the prolate-wave proxy strongly enough, under a source-defined normalization and cofinal cutoff regime, to force locally uniform convergence of the corresponding Fourier transforms/regularized determinants to the exact Riemann Xi function on a root-relevant domain. The atom explicitly separates ground-state simplicity/evenness, finite-N truncation convergence, prolate-to-Weil eigenvector stability, analytic transform control, normalization, and joint-limit order.
structural_coordinates: CCM Theorem 5.10 gives a self-adjoint finite/restricted operator and an entire regularized determinant proportional to the Fourier transform of the lowest truncated Weil-form eigenvector, conditional on that eigenvalue being simple with an even eigenvector

CCM Section 7 proves the Fourier transform of the prolate proxy k_lambda converges to Xi uniformly on closed substrips of |Im z|<1/2, but Section 8 states that proving k_lambda approximates a scalar multiple of the true lowest Weil-form eigenfunction xi_lambda is still missing
small Rayleigh value or small proxy discrepancy alone does not identify an eigenvector unless a quantitative spectral-separation/conditioning coordinate is controlled

the relevant source-side stability quantity can be organized as a residual-to-gap problem: approximate-eigenvector residual or Rayleigh excess must be compared with the spectral gap separating the ground state from the next mode
finite-dimensional truncation N and physical/arithmetic cutoff lambda are different approximation coordinates; the cofinal regime and order/path independence must be explicit
the normalization delta_N(xi)=1 or xi_lambda(lambda)=1 is load-bearing because determinant convergence is only meaningful up to zero-free factors unless a canonical normalization is fixed
Fourier/Mellin transform convergence on a strip requires weighted physical-space control strong enough for compact-uniform analytic convergence, not merely L2 closeness on expanding intervals
the target-side Hurwitz/Rouche step is already understood conditionally; this atom is source-side and must not count target-side zero transport as evidence for the missing source estimate
simple/even ground-state existence, gap positivity, proxy residual control, truncation convergence, and Xi identification are non-compensatory obligations
numerical agreement of low eigenvalues or proxy profiles can guide falsifiers but cannot replace a uniform source-side theorem
equivalent_formulations: prove a source-side bound dist(normalized k_lambda, span{xi_lambda}) -> 0 with a rate strong enough to imply locally uniform convergence of Fourier transforms on each closed substrip |Im z|<=1/2-delta
prove a quantitative approximate-ground-state theorem for QW_lambda in which a computable residual or Rayleigh excess for k_lambda divided by the actual ground-state spectral gap tends to zero

prove fixed-lambda convergence of normalized lowest eigenvectors xi_(lambda,N) to xi_lambda as N->infinity, then prove lambda->infinity convergence of xi_lambda to the prolate/Riemann proxy in a weighted topology that controls analytic transforms

falsify the determinant route by showing that the natural proxy can have vanishing Rayleigh excess while the relevant ground-state gap collapses too quickly, so eigenvector identification does not follow

replace direct eigenvector comparison by a source-defined compactness-plus-uniqueness argument: every normalized subsequential ground-state limit satisfies a characterization whose unique solution is the prolate/Riemann proxy
solved_analogues: Davis–Kahan/Kato-type perturbation and approximate-eigenvector estimates for isolated self-adjoint eigenvalues: eigenvector/subspace stability is controlled by perturbation or residual size relative to spectral separation
Rayleigh–Ritz/Galerkin convergence for isolated ground states of closed lower-bounded forms when the approximation spaces form a suitable core and the target eigenvalue remains isolated
Hurwitz/Rouche compact-uniform zero transport once the source-normalized analytic convergence and nonzero target have already been proved
near_solved_analogues: Connes–Consani–Moscovici 2025: finite/restricted self-adjoint/real-zero determinant mechanism is rigorous under simple-even hypotheses; Section 7 proves the prolate proxy transform tends to Xi; Section 8 leaves true Weil-ground-state identification open

Connes–van Suijlekom 2025: general lower-bounded self-adjoint quadratic-form mechanism generating entire functions with only real zeros under a simple isolated even ground state, but not the zeta-specific global identification

prolate time-frequency concentration theory: the relevant low prolate modes have strong asymptotic localization and explicit spectral separation information, but QW_lambda is not the prolate operator and the transfer needs a theorem relating their ground-state geometries

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A model output can fit observations with tiny residual while the inferred latent mode remains unstable when two modes are nearly degenerate; state identification requires residual size to be small relative to a stability/conditioning scale.
common_abstraction: small forward residual versus latent-state identification
source_to_target_mapping: forward residual -> QW_lambda approximate-eigenvector residual or Rayleigh excess of k_lambda
latent mode -> true lowest even Weil-form eigenvector xi_lambda
conditioning scale -> spectral gap above the ground state
stable estimator -> source-side eigenvector identification theorem
shared_constraints: the residual and stability scale must be independently defined
the same norm/space must be used for numerator and denominator
a nearly-degenerate hostile control must be rejected
disanalogies: RH has no measurement noise or statistical estimator
the QW_lambda gap and domain properties are arithmetic/operator theorems, not empirical calibration parameters
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Do not use small proxy error, small energy, or visual/numerical profile agreement as ground-state identification unless the argument exposes and controls the relevant spectral conditioning denominator.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: Freeze a two-mode self-adjoint near-degeneracy negative control and require any proposed QW_lambda proxy certificate to fail when residual/Rayleigh error tends to zero no faster than the ground-state gap; then prove the corresponding numerator and gap bounds for the actual source family.
